name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
title: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
answer: Impairment of unique digital assets covers how entities test and write down the carrying value of non-fungible tokens, digital collectibles, virtual land, in-game items, and similar one-of-a-kind intangible assets recorded on a blockchain. Unlike fungible cryptoassets, these items lack an active market with identical units, so fair value is often estimated from recent sales of comparable assets or from the last transaction price adjusted for liquidity. The page addresses recognition of impairment losses, reversal rules where applicable, and disclosure of assumptions.

sections.body: Impairment of unique digital assets covers how entities test and write down the carrying value of non-fungible tokens, digital collectibles, virtual land, in-game items, and similar one-of-a-kind intangible assets recorded on a blockchain. Unlike fungible cryptoassets, these items lack an active market with identical units, so fair value is often estimated from recent sales of comparable assets or from the last transaction price adjusted for liquidity. The page addresses recognition of impairment losses, reversal rules where applicable, and disclosure of assumptions.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on accounting ledgers that integrate blockchain explorers, marketplaces, and valuation feeds for unique token identifiers. Because each asset is distinct, systems must map token IDs and contract addresses to asset registers, then pull sale history and listing data from platforms where the asset trades. Many teams use spreadsheets or niche subledger tools rather than general ERP modules, since standard crypto accounting software often assumes fungible units.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Impairment testing for unique digital assets typically follows a cost-less-impairment model under many GAAP frameworks, meaning the asset is written down when its estimated recoverable amount falls below carrying value, but upward revaluation is not permitted until disposal. Practitioners identify triggering events such as a sustained drop in floor prices, loss of access to the private key, or a marketplace delisting, then estimate fair value using a market approach with comparable sales. The loss is recognized in profit or loss and the new carrying amount becomes the basis for future tests.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on custody, provenance, and the reliability of valuation evidence. A unique digital asset can be impaired by loss of the private key, a smart contract vulnerability, or a legal challenge to the token's authenticity, so impairment testing must consider whether the holder still controls the asset and whether the underlying metadata remains accessible. Accounting policy should document which marketplaces and price sources are acceptable, how to treat wash trades or non-arm's length sales, and who approves impairment charges. Provenance records on-chain can support existence and ownership but do not by themselves establish fair value.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The practice is moving toward more granular impairment triggers and better tooling for tracking floor prices and comparable sales across fragmented NFT marketplaces. As accounting standard setters clarify guidance for crypto intangibles, unique digital assets may shift toward fair value or revaluation models in some jurisdictions, which would change the one-way impairment pattern. Firms are also beginning to separate the asset from associated rights, such as royalties or access tokens, so impairment tests may become more modular.
